body.statement: For every supported-row vector \(eta\in Cn\) and every \(q\in[0,1]\), \(|H(eta,q)-H(etahat,q)|\le\delta\). Consequently, \(\Pr(\{H(eta0,q):q\in[0,1]\}\subseteq Kn)\ge 1-\alpha\). The reported \(Kn\) is a conservative confidence enclosure and is not asserted to equal the exact projection \(\bigcup_{eta\in Cn}H(eta,[0,1])\).
body.justification: This separates structural nonidentification from sampling uncertainty while respecting repeated uses of each shared row.
body.gap: Duarte et al. optimize over general confidence constraints; no surveyed RSCM result supplies the labeled occurrence-coupling radius for a shared row used repeatedly in one target grounding.
body.consumer: The N3 traffic point can be reported with both its exact population support range and a finite-sample outer enclosure for noisy supported rows.
body.proof_tex:
If \(Cn=\varnothing\), the first assertion is vacuous and \(Kn=[0,1]\).  Assume henceforth that \(Cn\neq\varnothing\), so the deterministic feasible \(etahat\in Cn\) is defined.  For any \(eta\in Cn\) and supported row \(r\), the box constraints give
\[
 \frac12\sum_y|eta_{r,y}-etahat_{r,y}|
 \leq \frac12\sum_y\max\!\left\{|\ell_{r,y}-etahat_{r,y}|,
 |u_{r,y}-etahat_{r,y}|\right\}.
\]
The left side is the total-variation distance between the two categorical rows and is at most one.  Hence it is at most \(\epsilon_r\).

Fix \(q\in[0,1]\).  Couple target draws under \((eta,q)\) and \((etahat,q)\) in a topological order of the intervened acyclic ground graph.  Intervened nodes are equal.  As long as all earlier nonintervened outputs agree, the current node has the same parent tuple and therefore the same type--context key in both systems.  If that key is \(rstar\), use identical draws from \((1-q,q)\).  If it is a supported row \(r\), put \(c_y=\min\{eta_{r,y},etahat_{r,y}\}\) and \(s=\sum_yc_y\).  Assign probability \(c_y\) to the equal pair \((y,y)\).  If \(s<1\), assign the residual pair \((y,z)\) probability
\[
 \frac{(eta_{r,y}-c_y)(etahat_{r,z}-c_z)}{1-s}.
\]
For each category at least one residual factor is zero, so this residual law has no diagonal mass; direct summation verifies the two prescribed marginals.  Its disagreement probability is \(1-s=\frac12\sum_y|eta_{r,y}-etahat_{r,y}|\leq\epsilon_r\).  Fresh coupling randomness at each node preserves the prescribed conditional marginal in each target system.

Let \(A_v\) be the event that the first disagreement occurs at node \(v\).  These events are disjoint.  Conditional on no earlier disagreement, the bound above applies to the row label at \(v\).  Summing over nodes and grouping their certified labels, with \(m_r\) an upper bound on the number of occurrences labeled \(r\), yields
\[
 \Pr\!\left(\bigcup_v A_v\right)=\sum_v\Pr(A_v)
 \leq\sum_r m_r\epsilon_r.
\]
The bound is also at most one after clipping, so it is at most \(\delta\).  The indicators of \(B\) in the two coupled target systems can differ only after some node disagreement.  Therefore the elementary coupling inequality gives
\[
 |H(eta,q)-H(etahat,q)|\leq\Pr\!\left(\bigcup_v A_v\right)\leq\delta.
\]
This is uniform in \(eta\in Cn\) and \(q\in[0,1]\).

Let \(E_n=\{eta0\in Cn\}\).  Joint box coverage gives \(\Pr(E_n)\geq1-\alpha\).  On \(E_n\), the uniform inequality implies, for every \(q\in[0,1]\),
\[
 Lhat-\delta\leq H(eta0,q)\leq Uhat+\delta.
\]
Since \(H\) is a probability, clipping the left endpoint at zero and the right endpoint at one preserves the inclusion.  Thus
\[
 \{H(eta0,q):q\in[0,1]\}\subseteq Kn
\]
on \(E_n\), and the asserted probability is at least \(1-\alpha\).  Sampling-context positivity makes the population conditional rows in \(eta0\) well defined, while the joint-box assumption supplies the only probabilistic coverage step.  The proof optimizes only the center polynomial in \(q\) and then inflates uniformly; it nowhere asserts that this interval is the exact multivariate projection over \(Cn\).
